changes.evidence: In episode 11 Mar-Vell is already living undercover on Earth as Dr. Wendy Lawson of the U.S. Air Force. She only wears her old Kree Starforce uniform, and the wiki lists Starforce as '(formerly)'. Her Starforce service comes before the title.

Her Culver University IT internship is earlier backstory (the wiki's 'Early Life', Culver marked '(formerly)'). In episode 12 she is only a Stark Industries intern, and she just uses a trick she learned at Culver.

Episode 16: Odin strips Hela of her power and banishes her from Asgard to Earth, shown on screen. The Ten Rings capture her and she escapes. She finds refuge in Ta Lo and trains under Jiayi until she masters their ways, then leaves to face Odin. Odin yields the throne and she becomes Queen of Asgard, allied with the Ten Rings.

Episode 13: a drunk racer on Sakaar, she helps Tony overthrow the Grandmaster and the crowd crowns her King of Sakaar. She accepts and names Korg her special counsel. The record never shows her taking Sakaar's throne.

Episode 13: Korg starts as a prisoner forced to race in the Grand Prix and joins Tony's revolt. After the Grandmaster falls, King Valkyrie makes him her special counsel and he accepts, so he joins the new Sakaar regime.

Episode 25: Ultron, alone in his dead universe, agrees to atone, absorbs the shard and takes Kahhori, Byrdie and Storm to rescue Carter and the Watcher. The wiki's section for this is 'Joining the Guardians of the Multiverse'. He dies in the finale fighting beside them, and death is not a departure.

Episode 21 opens with Alexei on a Soviet mission with the Winter Soldier (the wiki lists Soviet Armed Forces as '(formerly)'). He breaks from it, goes on the run and lives as 'Bob Toledo'. Bill Foster of S.H.I.E.L.D. offers him a job and he accepts (the wiki section is 'Recruited by S.H.I.E.L.D.'), and 21 years later he is an Avenger. Soviet Armed Forces is the group Dreykov's record uses in this episode.

owner_calls.question: She is court merlin to the Asgardian Royal Family and turns on King Thor in the episode 17 climax. Which stages should she have? The current 'Independent' misses her service to the crown.
options: [["Asgard", "What If...? S2"], ["Independent", "What If...? S2"]] (serves the crown, then defects)
[["Asgard", "What If...? S2"], ["The Avengers", "What If...? S2"]] (defects to Carter's team; the wiki lists her as an ally, not a member)
[["Asgard", "(from the start)"]] (betraying Thor once to save reality is not leaving the court)
owner_calls.evidence: Wiki: 'appointed in the role of advisor to the Asgardian Royal Family'. She 'betrayed her king, restraining him' so Carter could use the Scepter. The infobox affiliation is blank.

owner_calls.question: Sir Nicholas is a knight of the Asgardian Royal Family's military. He secretly helps Carter and openly betrays King Thor in episode 17. Which stages should he have?
options: [["Asgard", "What If...? S2"], ["Independent", "What If...? S2"]] (serves the crown, then defects)
owner_calls.evidence: Wiki: 'Sir Nick Fury served the Asgardian Royal Family as a knight'. 'Fury betrayed his king' and stole the Scepter for Tony Stark. The infobox has no affiliation, and his 'Sir' title is marked '(formerly)'.

owner_calls.question: By the end of episode 23 every other Alliance member is dead (everything after Vision's defeat was Beck's illusion), and the wiki marks her Alliance affiliation '(formerly)'. Does the wiped-out Alliance count as a team ending?
options: Keep [["The Alliance", "(from the start)"]] (death of teammates is not a departure)
owner_calls.evidence: She learns her comrades are dead, kills Beck alone, then projects the Avengers logo into the sky. The infobox reads 'Alliance (formerly)'.

owner_calls.question: In episode 15 conquistadors capture Wáhta, shackle him and put him on a ship to Spain, and Kahhori frees him in the same episode. Should this short captivity be a stage, or is the current record fine?
options: Add a captive stage and a return to Mohawk within What If...? S2
owner_calls.evidence: The wiki section 'Taken by the Conquistadores' covers the capture. He is freed before the episode ends and stays Mohawk.

owner_calls.question: In episode 12 Hammer's men hold Darcy hostage for a short time before Freak frees her. Should this be a captive stage, or is it too brief (separate from the Culver fix above)?
options: Add a Hammer Industries captive stage, then return to Stark Industries
owner_calls.evidence: Rusty and Sergei capture her in the server room. She is handcuffed next to Maria Hill, then Freak frees her in the same scene sequence.
